'''Sergei Voloshin''' (born February 18, 1953) is a Russian-American experimental high-energy nuclear physicist and Professor of Physics at [[Wayne State University]]. He is best known for his work on event-by-event physics in heavy ion collisions.

==Career==
Sergei Voloshin studied physics at [[Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]], where he completed his PhD in [[nuclear physics]] in 1980 and became a faculty member at the Department of [[Theoretical physics|Theoretical Physics]]. During the period from 1992 to 1999 he was a visiting scientist at the [[University of Pittsburgh]], Physikalische Institute ([[University of Heidelberg]]) and [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] (LBNL) where he worked on anisotropic flow and event-by-event physics in nuclear collisions at [[Super Proton Synchrotron|SPS]] and RHIC. In 1999 Dr. Voloshin joined the Department of Physics and Astronomy at [[Wayne State University]].

==Work==
One of the best known Voloshin's contribution is the analysis and interpretation of the so-called anisotropic flow in heavy ion collisions.<ref>[http://prc.aps.org/abstract/PRC/v58/i3/p1671_1 Methods for analyzing anisotropic flow in relativistic nuclear collisions] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130414004246/http://prc.aps.org/abstract/PRC/v58/i3/p1671_1 |date=2013-04-14 }}", A. M. Poskanzer and S. A. Voloshin, ''Physical Review C'' 58, (1998) 1671–1678.</ref><ref>"[http://inspirehep.net/record/374777 Flow study in relativistic nuclear collisions by Fourier expansion of Azimuthal particle distributions]", S. Voloshin, Y. Zhang, ''[[Zeitschrift für Physik]]'' 70 (1996) 665-672.</ref> He played a leading role in the discovery of the strong elliptic flow at RHIC.<ref>[http://prl.aps.org/abstract/PRL/v86/i3/p402_1 Elliptic Flow in Au+Au Collisions at √sNN = 130GeV]," STAR Collaboration, ''[[Physical Review Letters]]'' 86, (2001) 402–407.</ref> Large elliptic flow, consistent with calculations from ideal hydrodynamics, was a key to the concept of strongly interacting Quark Gluon Plasma, a new form of matter discovered at RHIC. The idea of the constituent quark scaling, proposed by Voloshin, and its observation at RHIC is widely regarded as a proof for a deconfinement [[phase transition]]. His recent research interests include studies of possible local parity violation in strong interaction in heavy ion collisions.

Dr. Voloshin is a member of the [[STAR detector|STAR Collaboration]] performing experiments at [[Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider]] (RHIC) at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] (BNL), and the [[ALICE experiment|ALICE Collaboration]] at [[Large Hadron Collider]] (LHC) at [[CERN]].

==Honors==
*Elected a Fellow of [[American Physical Society]] in 2008 "for numerous seminal contributions to the methods and interpretation of collective flow in relativistic nuclear collisions”.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://newsroom.wayne.edu/news/2009/03/23/wayne-state-physics-professor-honored-by-american-physical-society-3201|title=Wayne State physics professor honored by American Physical Society|date=May 23, 2009|publisher=Wayne State University|access-date=January 16, 2019}}</ref>
*Inducted to [[Wayne State University]]'s Academy of Scholars in 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://physics.clas.wayne.edu/news/professor-sergei-voloshin-elected-member-of-wsu-academy-of-scholars-27030|title=Professor Sergei Voloshin Elected Member of WSU Academy of Scholars|publisher=Wayne State University|date=April 20, 2012|access-date=January 16, 2019}}</ref>
